answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by requiring a small, nonrefundable deposit that is slashed if independent audits find coordinated identities repeating the same claims or transactions. Auditors compare behavior across time, not just profile details, so an attacker cannot cheaply gain weight by minting accounts. The deposit makes every fake identity consume scarce capital; spreading votes across a river of aliases multiplies the cost, while a legitimate haven can preserve reputation. A changing pigment in the audit record can mark reviewed evidence without revealing private identity.
